subject: MAP draft: SLA sampling plan, statistical acceptance tests, and rollback playbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@medsync.ai>, MedSync Ops <ops@medsync.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft: SLA sampling plan, statistical acceptance tests, and rollback playbook

Priya — attaching a short draft of the MAP section focused on how we validate SLA targets during the evaluation phase. High-level asks: please confirm (1) the two business-critical flows to be sampled (appointment creation and claims enrichment), (2) your comfort with the proposed statistical tolerance (5% false positive ceiling across sampled requests), and (3) whether the Ops team can run the suggested production-like sampling for two business days during the pilot window.

Quick summary of what’s inside the attachments: 1) acceptance_matrix.xlsx — per-flow pass/fail criteria, sample size, and allowed failure modes; 2) sampling_plan.pdf — how we collect telemetry, anonymize PHI, and compute the SLA-sample stats.

Key decision we need by EOD Wednesday 5/11 so we can lock the canary configuration for the pilot on 5/14. If we don’t get signoff we’ll default to the conservative plan (smaller canary, longer observation period), which pushes close by ~1 week.

Notes on rollback: we propose an automated rollback if the 30-minute rolling error rate exceeds 2x baseline OR if latency P95 spikes above 2s over baseline for three consecutive 10-minute windows. That’s conservative but keeps MedSync service safe while we ramp.

Attachments: acceptance_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), sampling_plan.pdf (doc stub)

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@medsync.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft: SLA sampling plan, statistical acceptance tests, and rollback playbook

Ben / Priya — quick questions after reviewing the draft:

- Sample sizing: acceptance_matrix.xlsx uses a two-day window with N=3,000 per flow. Priya, do you have any seasonal traffic concerns that would bias the sample? If MedSync has a predictable batch at 03:00 UTC, we should avoid sampling only during peak or only during that batch window.

- Tolerance framing: we used a 5% FP cap and a separate P95 latency threshold. Would you prefer a combined composite score (weighted FP + latency) instead? That makes the canary decision easier but is more complex to explain to procurement.

- Data handling: sampling_plan.pdf calls for on-the-wire redaction then server-side hashing. Ops team, can your team run a one-hour redaction smoke test on the staging queue to validate the pipeline? Small ask but prevents surprises.

I can propose a revised canary size if Priya confirms traffic shape.

—Jordan
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@medsync.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSync Ops <ops@medsync.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft: SLA sampling plan, statistical acceptance tests, and rollback playbook

Thanks Ben — and thanks Jordan. Overall this looks good and aligns with our internal risk appetite. A few specifics from Ops and product: 

- Confirmed flows: appointment creation and claims enrichment — yes. We also want one lightweight negative-control flow (patient lookup) included in sampling to sanity-check false positives.

- Traffic note: we do have a nightly ingestion at 02:45–03:20 UTC. Please ensure the sampling plan stratifies by hour so we capture both batch and interactive traffic.

- Tolerance: product prefers a single composite acceptance score (60% weight for FP rate, 40% for latency) — easier for the execs to sign off. Can you reflect that in the matrix? The 5% cap for FP as a hard failure is fine as a safety override.

- Ops commit: we can run the redaction hash test in staging next Tuesday (5/17). We can also enable a short production sample on 5/14 for 4 hours if Redwood provides the sampling token and a clear rollback trigger.

I’ve attached a short annotated version of the sampling_plan.pdf with inline comments (returning via reply).

—Priya
Director of Product Operations | MedSync
priya@medsync.ai | +1 (415) 555-1972

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@medsync.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft: SLA sampling plan, statistical acceptance tests, and rollback playbook

Great — thanks for the quick review and the edits, Priya. Action items and confirmed plan: 

1) We will update acceptance_matrix.xlsx to include the composite score (60% FP, 40% P95 latency) with an FP hard-fail at 5%. Expect updated spreadsheet by EOD 5/13.
2) Redwood will provision a sampling token and short-run canary config for 5/14 (4-hour production sample).
3) MedSync Ops will run the staging redaction smoke test on 5/17; please share results in the Drive folder.
4) Canary rollback triggers (finalized): automated rollback if 30-min rolling error rate > 2x baseline OR composite score falls below 0.78 OR P95 latency > baseline + 2s for three consecutive 10-min windows.

I’ve created a short decision radar for close timing: if the 5/14 sample looks clean we move to a 5/21 extended pilot and target commercial close the week of 5/28. If we see issues that require rework, we’ll treat the outcome as "needs mitigation" and re-run sampling after fixes (likely +1–2 weeks).

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-redwood-maps-medSync (updated spreadsheet will land here). HubSpot: 748392.

Attachments referenced: acceptance_matrix.xlsx (will be replaced with updated version), sampling_plan.pdf (annotated).

Thanks — looking forward to the staging smoke test results and the 5/14 canary.

Ben Carter
